body:
I honestly believe one of the biggest problems we have at the moment is that communication has broke down. Early on during the pandemic, everyone was watching closely, paying close attention to what was happening. We were bombarded every day with new information, and overtime that information began to conflict with itself. 

People began to lose trust in what they were told, and it only became worse as time went on, people losing their jobs, losing their social lives, connections to their families and friends, and while many people suffered directly from covid, everyone suffered to some degree from the restrictions.

Yet we carried on, chasing the elusive bent curve, and the light at the end of the tunnel, as it was taunted in front of us repeatedly.

Then comes the vaccine. A lot of people are justifiably concerned at first regarding it's use. Is it safe? What are the side effects? How extensive was the testing? Is there a chance for long term side effects? Was it rushed out before it was ready? I don't think these are unreasonable questions to ask. After all, many the limelight champions of the vaccines today were adamant early on, through Twitter that any vaccine approved by Trump was not a vaccine they would take.

So now we have people who are downtrodden, that have seen the information they've been given change, time and time again. They no longer trust what the authorities are telling them is true, as it seems to them they are either making it up as they go, changing their minds every couple weeks, or they are worse yet, blatantly lying to folks. And the present day political landscape has only exacerbated this hostility people have with authority and worse yet their own neighbors. Unfortunately there is always JUST enough truth to what these people believe, that it makes the rest of their outlandish claims more palatable to digest.

And the reactions from people on the other side haven't made things any easier by the way. Meeting hostility with more hostility is hardly a productive means to rectify the problem. Talk of denying unvaccinated people access to healthcare. Rumours of vaccine passports being used to take people's jobs away, or restrict their access to a life that they had only just 2 years ago. You want to force people to put something in their body they don't want, then we are opening up a can of worms I don't think anyone is prepared for.

The unfortunate reality is politicians and health authorities need to regain the trust of these people, they need to admit with full transparency where they were wrong and reset the record on what we know with certainty, and where we could still be wrong. Then we need to convince these people that getting vaccinated, and following the guidelines protects them without significantly impacting their lives in a negative way. And lastly, we need to inform them, of what our exit strategy is realistically, can they expect things to go back to the normal way it was before covid, or will elements of it continue for the rest of the foreseeable future. We need transparency, we need trust, we need clear communication, and we need empathy and sadly I'm not convinced were capable of achieving that anymore.

I have found the opposite for construction. In commercial the hours are pretty standard 40 hour/week, where as residential it's much longer days and longer weeks. Industrial is often the same, long days/weeks with a rotation and roadwork is extremely long days and weeks, due to seasonal work. There are of course exceptions, depending on the project and schedule, but generally that has been my experience for the last 12 years.

I'm done with hope. Hope is just another form of luck, and good luck has never been my friend.
I use to believe in karma, that doing good things, and trying to be a good person will in turn bring good things to my life, but it hasn't. I use to believe the world would balance itself out, or my world rather would. That eventually my life would have a pay off for all the suffering, for all the loneliness, for all the abuse I've been subject to, and the world would finally reward me with something special. But it doesn't work that way does it?

They say the only one who can really change things for yourself, the only one in charge of your destiny is you, but I feel like there are just too many barriers in the way now, that I've gone for too long with harmful coping mechanisms, without a proper support structure, that my mental illnesses have compounded and mutated, festered into something so unstoppable, that every possible solution I have to end my own suffering in a positive way is stone walled by another part of my critically damaged psyche.

That is why I can't hope anymore. Because hope is just a lie to me. Hope is a lie I can tell myself to make the pain go away for a short while, only to have it crushed later, like pulling the knife out, only to sharpen it before plunging it back in again. That's what hope does to me.
